common_name: Pink Impression Tulip (Deep Rose-Pink Darwin Hybrid Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Pink Impression is a Darwin hybrid tulip with huge, globe-shaped, deep rose-pink flowers on sturdy stems.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Pink Impression, a Darwin hybrid tulip bred for extra-large flowers on strong, tall stems, produces huge, globe-shaped blooms in deep, saturated rose-pink that have made it one of the most widely planted pink tulips for mass displays and cut flowers. Darwin hybrids like Pink Impression also tend to perennialize somewhat better than many other tulip types in climates with adequate winter chill, though in mild-winter zone 8-9 gardens they are still usually most reliable treated as a fresh fall planting.

common_name: Golden Apeldoorn Tulip (Golden-Yellow Darwin Hybrid with Black Base)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Golden Apeldoorn is a golden-yellow sport of the classic red Apeldoorn Darwin hybrid tulip, with a black basal blotch.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Golden Apeldoorn, a golden-yellow sport of the classic red Apeldoorn Darwin hybrid, bears large, clear yellow blooms marked with a contrasting black basal blotch at the center, on strong, tall stems typical of the Darwin hybrid group. Darwin hybrids like Golden Apeldoorn also tend to perennialize somewhat better than many other tulip types in climates with adequate winter chill, though in mild-winter zone 8-9 gardens they are still usually most reliable treated as a fresh fall planting.

common_name: Kees Nelis Tulip (Fire-Red Triumph Tulip Edged Golden Yellow)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Kees Nelis is a Triumph-class tulip with fire-red petals edged in golden yellow, blooming midseason.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Kees Nelis, a Triumph-class tulip, bears vivid fire-red petals crisply edged in golden yellow, a bold bicolor combination blooming in midseason on sturdy, medium-height stems typical of the versatile Triumph group, which bridges early singles and late Darwin hybrids in bloom timing. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Don Quichotte Tulip (Vivid Cerise-Pink Triumph Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Don Quichotte is a Triumph-class tulip with vivid cerise-pink flowers, a good cultivar for forcing indoors as well as garden display.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Don Quichotte, a Triumph-class tulip, bears vivid, saturated cerise-pink flowers on sturdy, medium-height stems, blooming in midseason, and is noted as a particularly reliable cultivar for forcing into early bloom indoors in addition to standard garden and landscape display. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Abu Hassan Tulip (Mahogany-Red Triumph Tulip Edged Bright Yellow)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Abu Hassan is a Triumph-class tulip with mahogany-red petals edged in bright yellow, blooming midseason.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Abu Hassan, a Triumph-class tulip, bears rich mahogany-red petals crisply edged in bright golden yellow, a warm, autumnal bicolor combination blooming in midseason on sturdy, medium-height stems typical of the versatile Triumph group. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Jan Reus Tulip (Rich Wine-Purple-Red Triumph Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Jan Reus is a Triumph-class tulip with rich wine-purple-red goblet-shaped flowers, blooming midseason.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Jan Reus, a Triumph-class tulip, bears rich, deep wine-purple-red goblet-shaped flowers on sturdy, medium-height stems, blooming in midseason with a dark, saturated color that pairs well with lighter-toned tulip companions in a mixed spring bulb display. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Fancy Frills Tulip (White Fringed Tulip Feathered Pink)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Fancy Frills is a Fringed-class tulip with white petals feathered pink at the edges, blooming late in the season.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Fancy Frills bears white petals delicately feathered with pink at the edges, each petal margin finely crystalline-fringed in the distinctive texture of the Fringed tulip class, blooming late in the tulip season for an extended spring bulb display when paired with earlier-blooming cultivars. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Davenport is a Fringed-class tulip with deep cherry-red blooms and fine crystalline fringe, blooming late in the season.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Davenport bears deep, rich cherry-red blooms with fine, crystalline fringe edging each petal, the delicate icy-textured margin distinctive to the Fringed tulip class, blooming late in the tulip season for an extended spring bulb display when paired with earlier-blooming cultivars. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Blue Heron bears rich violet-purple flowers with a finely crystalline-fringed petal edge distinctive to the Fringed tulip class, blooming late in the tulip season for an extended spring bulb display when paired with earlier-blooming cultivars. Its cool, deep purple tone provides strong contrast against yellow, orange, or white companion tulips. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens.

common_name: Spring Green Tulip (Ivory-White Viridiflora Tulip with Green Flame)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Spring Green is a Viridiflora-class tulip with ivory-white petals marked by a central green feathered flame, blooming late in the season.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Spring Green, one of the most popular Viridiflora-class tulips, bears creamy ivory-white petals streaked down the center with a feathered flame of green, the distinctive partial-green coloring that defines the Viridiflora group, blooming late in the tulip season with a soft, subtle look that pairs beautifully with nearly any garden color scheme. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: China Town Tulip (Pink-Cream Viridiflora Tulip with Variegated Foliage)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; China Town is a Viridiflora-class tulip with soft pink-and-cream flowers marked by a green flame, and unusually also bears variegated foliage.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. China Town bears soft pink-and-cream petals streaked down the center with a feathered flame of green, the distinctive partial-green coloring that defines the Viridiflora group, and unusually for a tulip, the foliage itself is also variegated with cream-white margins, giving this cultivar ornamental interest even before the flowers open. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Artist Tulip (Salmon-Orange Viridiflora Tulip Streaked Purple and Green)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Artist is a Viridiflora-class tulip with salmon-orange petals streaked with purple and green, blooming late in the season.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Artist bears an unusually complex, painterly blend of salmon-orange petals streaked with purple and green, the multicolor pattern giving each flower a hand-painted look that has made this cultivar a favorite among gardeners seeking something beyond a solid-colored tulip. Its shorter, more compact stature fits containers and the front of a mixed spring bulb border well. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Mount Tacoma Tulip (Pure White Peony-Form Double Late Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Mount Tacoma is a Double Late (peony-flowered) class tulip with pure white, fully double blooms, flowering late in the season.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in a site sheltered from strong wind, since the large double flower heads can be heavy. Mount Tacoma bears large, densely ruffled, pure white double blooms with the full, rounded form of a garden peony rather than a typical single tulip flower, opening late in the season and providing a clean, elegant counterpart to the blush-pink Angelique within the same Double Late class. As with most tulips, treat as an annual fall-planted bulb display in mild-winter Southern gardens rather than expecting reliable long-term perennializing.

common_name: Spellbinder Daffodil (Sulphur-Yellow Trumpet Fading to White)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil; Spellbinder is a Division 1 trumpet daffodil that opens sulphur-yellow and fades to white as the bloom ages, giving a color-changing display.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile soil, and allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally after bloom rather than cutting or braiding it, since the leaves recharge the bulb for next year's flowers. Spellbinder, a Division 1 large trumpet daffodil, opens a soft sulphur-yellow and gradually fades to near-white as the flower ages, so a single clump displays a range of tones from fresh yellow buds to pale mature blooms all at once. It blooms in midseason and is completely deer- and rodent-resistant like other daffodils.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Daffodil Varieties for Gulf South Gardens

common_name: Merlin Daffodil (White with Small Red-Rimmed Cup)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil; Merlin is a Division 3 small-cup daffodil with a white perianth and a small greenish-yellow cup rimmed in red-orange, blooming late in the season.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile soil, and allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally after bloom rather than cutting or braiding it. Merlin, a Division 3 small-cup daffodil, bears broad white petals surrounding a small, flat, greenish-yellow cup crisply rimmed in vivid red-orange, an eye-catching color contrast on a daintier bloom than the large-trumpet types. It flowers late in the daffodil season, extending the display when paired with earlier-blooming cultivars, and is completely deer- and rodent-resistant.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Daffodil Varieties for Gulf South Gardens

common_name: Replete Daffodil (Double Apricot-Pink and White Daffodil)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil; Replete is a Division 4 double daffodil with apricot-pink petaloids mixed among white outer petals, blooming late in the season.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile soil, and allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally after bloom rather than cutting or braiding it. Replete, a Division 4 double daffodil, bears full, ruffled blooms mixing soft apricot-pink petaloids among broader white outer petals, an unusual and delicate color combination among double daffodil cultivars, blooming late in the season for an extended display. Its fully double form provides a fuller, rose-like look distinct from single-flowered daffodil types, and it is completely deer- and rodent-resistant.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Daffodil Varieties for Gulf South Gardens

common_name: Quail Daffodil (Deep Golden Fragrant Multi-Flowered Jonquilla Daffodil)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil; Quail is a Division 7 jonquilla daffodil bearing deep golden-yellow, strongly fragrant flowers, several per stem, blooming late in the season.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile soil, and allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally after bloom rather than cutting or braiding it. Quail, a Division 7 jonquilla daffodil, bears clusters of deep, rich golden-yellow flowers, several per stem, with the strong, sweet fragrance characteristic of jonquilla types, blooming late in the daffodil season. Jonquilla daffodils like Quail tend to have narrower, rush-like foliage and often perennialize especially well in warmer Southern gardens compared to large-trumpet hybrid types. It is completely deer- and rodent-resistant.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Daffodil Varieties for Gulf South Gardens

common_name: Cassata Daffodil (White with Frilled Yellow-to-White Split Cup)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil; Cassata is a Division 11 split-corona daffodil with a white perianth and a frilled, flattened yellow-to-white split cup that opens flat against the petals.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, moderately fertile soil, and allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally after bloom rather than cutting or braiding it. Cassata, a Division 11 split-corona (butterfly or collar) daffodil, bears a clean white perianth behind a frilled, flattened cup that starts golden yellow and fades toward white, the corona split into segments that lie open against the petals rather than forming the typical cup or trumpet shape, giving the flower an orchid-like or camellia-like appearance unlike any other daffodil division. It blooms in midseason and is completely deer- and rodent-resistant.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Daffodil Varieties for Gulf South Gardens
